external_entities.name: user's browser
external_entities.description: A user's browser outside the system's network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

processes.name: web application
processes.description: The web application serving browser traffic and putting jobs onto the message queue.
processes.source_excerpt: The web application does not do the heavy work itself. It puts jobs onto a message queue

processes.name: background worker process
processes.description: A background worker that picks up jobs and reads and writes the database.
processes.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work.

data_stores.name: message queue
data_stores.description: A queue holding jobs placed by the web application and picked up by the background worker.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue, and a background worker process picks them up

data_stores.name: database
data_stores.description: The database read and written by the background worker and used to keep application log records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database. The database is also where we keep the application's log records.

data_stores.name: web application config
data_stores.description: A config store containing the web application's settings and queue credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the web application has a web application config

data_stores.name: worker config
data_stores.description: A config store containing the worker's settings and database credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the worker has a worker config

data_flows.name: talks to application
data_flows.description: The user's browser talks to the web application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

data_flows.name: puts jobs
data_flows.description: The web application puts jobs onto the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue
data_flows.notes: The description does not say how the web application authenticates to the queue.

data_flows.name: picks up jobs
data_flows.description: The background worker picks jobs up from the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work.

data_flows.name: reads and writes
data_flows.description: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.notes: The description does not say how the worker authenticates to the database.
data_flows.data_description: database records and application log records

data_flows.name: reads settings
data_flows.description: The web application reads its settings and queue credentials from its config store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Both processes read their settings from a config store: the web application has a web application config

data_flows.name: reads settings
data_flows.description: The background worker reads its settings and database credentials from its config store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Both processes read their settings from a config store: ... the worker has a worker config.

trust_boundaries.name: public internet
trust_boundaries.description: The public internet where the user's browser is located outside the system's network.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

trust_boundaries.name: web tier
trust_boundaries.description: The tier where the web application runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the web application runs in our web tier.

trust_boundaries.name: backend tier
trust_boundaries.description: The tier behind the web tier containing the queue, worker and database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The queue, the worker and the database are all in the backend tier, behind the web tier.

assumptions.assumption: The user's browser is an external system rather than a human entity.
assumptions.basis: The named actor is a browser, which is software outside the system's control.
The user's browser reaches it across the public internet.

assumptions.assumption: The background worker is a non-web process.
assumptions.basis: It is described as a background worker process rather than an application presenting a web interface.

assumptions.assumption: The web application config is confidential.
assumptions.basis: The config store holds the web application's queue credentials.
The config store holds the worker's database credentials.
